text:
ellie: Quick heads-up — we plan to ship SDK v4.1.0 + a docs 'cookbook' refresh tomorrow morning (09:30 PT). Main changes: consolidation of timeout params and a small rename to the streaming flag. Details below.

sam: Can you summarize the actual param changes? Any breaking semantics?

ellie: Yes — two small surface changes: 1) `timeout_ms` + `deadline` are being unified into `deadline_ms` (milliseconds). 2) `stream` is being renamed to `enable_stream` to make boolean intent clearer. No behavior change other than names.

mohammed: Will old names still work? Our integration tests hit these keys directly in several SDK examples.

ellie: We'll include a migration shim in the SDK that accepts the old names and emits a single deprecation warning per process. Shim lives in client init and will translate to `deadline_ms` and `enable_stream`. Shim will be supported for 6 months. After that the SDK will raise a ConfigError when old keys are present.

jess: What about the hosted API? Do we need to coordinate server-side checks?

ellie: Hosted API will accept both keys for a 30-day transition window. We'll log traces when old keys are used and show a banner in the Console for tenants using deprecated params. After 30 days we will require the new names on the public API; internally we'll continue to support the mapping longer for compatibility with Dedicated/Private.

ryan: Any lint or CI failures we should watch for? Our docs linter runs on PRs and flags unknown config keys.

ellie: Good catch — we added a new docs-linter rule `DEPRECATE_PARAM_KEY` that will warn for the old keys. It will be 'warn' for the next two weeks, then bumped to 'error' in the docs pipeline. The SDK repo CI will allow the shim for now but also emit a soft warning in test logs.

docs-bot: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/421 — "Cookbook: consolidate timeout & streaming params" — includes updated snippets for Python/JS/Go and a migration example. Linter rule: DEPRECATE_PARAM_KEY (rule id: docs-325).

mohammed: Do the code examples include a migration helper? We should show the shim usage and a tiny CLI helper for bulk repo search/replace.

ellie: Yep — the cookbook has a "migration" recipe with a 3-line shim example and a `rwi-cli migrate-params` command that can scan JS/Python/Go snippets and either report or rewrite occurrences. It will be part of `rwi-cli@0.9.0`.

sam: Nice. We should prepare a short internal comms note for Support and Sales so they can explain the windows to customers.

ellie: Agreed — @release-bot will publish a changelog and an internal migration checklist. Public changelog entry will call out: SDK v4.1.0, 30-day hosted API dual-accept window, 6-month SDK shim, linter enforcement timeline, CLI helper.

release-bot: Draft changelog: "SDK v4.1.0 — param consolidation (timeout_ms|deadline -> deadline_ms), stream -> enable_stream, migration shim (6 months), hosted api dual-accept (30 days), docs linter schedule, rwi-cli migration tool." Link to internal checklist: https://internal.redwood/docs/migration-checklist-1767

jess: Can we add a short snippet in the Console release banner explaining how to opt into the stricter linting earlier? Some teams might prefer to fail fast.

ellie: Yes — we'll add a toggle in the Console under Docs > Settings: "Enforce deprecated param errors". Teams can flip it to 'error' and run CI to verify.

sam: Anything else? Rollout time tomorrow at 09:30 PT you said?

ellie: Correct. I'll post an email to #all at 09:00 PT with the timeline and a link to the migration checklist. Please review the PR if you have language concerns.

ryan: Reviewed the examples locally — looks good. One minor nit in Go snippets, sending a quick fix PR.

jess: :thumbsup:

ellie: Thanks everyone — ping me if you see any edge cases. We should have release notes + changelog up right after the deployment.
